R1D-bear-backcountry-0004.name: 180 m NW of Leiner River
R1D-bear-backcountry-0004.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R1D-bear-backcountry-0004.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2021 (5 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
S facing slope, 24 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Leiner River 180 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; Bow Only; no bow only season on the Gulf Islands in MU 1-1 (except Gabriola Island), in zone B of MU 1-5 (Map A12) or on Denman and Hornby Islands (MU 1-6)

plan: Drive: from City of Campbell River, about 125 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.94958, -126.65511, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.5 km E, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 995 m, about 210 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 360 m SE of the spot at 142 m (49.93253, -126.57868). Water: Leiner River 90 m NE (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-12, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R1D-bear-backcountry-0004.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 1-12: about 353 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.06 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

R1D-deer-backcountry-0001.name: 2.7 km S of Leiner River rec site
R1D-deer-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-1-014 unit V01d (official), 40 m S. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2006 (20 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHvm1): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
W facing slope, 17 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

flags.t: Route crosses provincial park: Weymer Creek Park. Hunting only where that park allows it, in open season. Check its bcparks.ca page (synopsis page 9, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: On Denman and Hornby Islands the season is Oct 5 to Dec 10. Part of MU 1-6 (Map A26) is 2 point or better; keep antlers with the species licence

Bow Only. no bow only season on the Gulf Islands in MU 1-1 (except Gabriola Island), in zone B of MU 1-5 (Map A12) or on Denman and Hornby Islands (MU 1-6). Part of MU 1-6 (Map A26) is 2 point or better
LEH (Limited Entry Hunting): draw only, not a general open season
No row in the Region 1 table, so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis). Mountain quail: printed 'No open season on mountain quail'.

Walk: 5.3 km NW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 943 m, about 200 min at 3 km/h.
